title: USMNT Player Ratings vs. Mexico: Two Stars Are Born in Dream Night for U.S. Soccer
subtitle: SI
paragraphs: By Roberto Casillas12:40 AM EDTJulian Hall (left) and Cavan Sullivan (second from left to right) stole the show vs. Mexico.  / Chris Coduto/Getty Images        The U.S. men’s national team enjoyed a fairytale Saturday night with a 3–0 win against arch-nemesis Mexico, thanks to a pair of goals from teenagers Julian Hall and Cavan Sullivan.

It wasn’t the easiest of starts for the USMNT, who struggled to string together passes to bypass Mexico’s aggressive press. Mauricio Pochettino’s men had to dig deep, but they slowly started to settle into the match.

When the Stars and Stripes finally managed to manufacture a sustained possession, they pounced. Alex Freeman freed a charging Giovanni Reyna who got away from his man and whipped a powerful cross that Raúl Rangel couldn’t handle, leaving the rebound on a platter for 18-year-old rising star Julian Hall to introduce himself under the bright lights of North America’s biggest rivalry to give the USMNT the lead 28 minutes in.

The USMNT improved in the second half, and just when Mexico seemed to get back in the game, it was 17-year-old wonderkid Cavan Sullivan’s turn to announce himself on the biggest stage. Sullivan intercepted an egregious Rangel pass, and without any hesitation, he kept his cool and lobbed a shot over the goalkeeper to double his side’s lead just past the hour mark.

Mexico completely collapsed, and Mateo Chávez was sent off after slapping Sebastian Berhalter. Then, Malik Tillman added the cherry on top of a sensational night with a powerful hit into the roof of the net in the 85th minute.

The Stars and Stripes categorically erased Mexico from the pitch in the second half and could’ve easily inflicted more harm. Still, in one of the greatest nights of Pochettino’s tenure, the Argentine boss got his first win in North America’s biggest rivalry and the USMNT’s 2030 cycle is off to to a perfect start.

Julian Hall’s dream start to his international career continued.  / Taylor Banner/USSF/Getty Images Pochettino’s side looked uncomfortable for much of the first half against an intense El Tri that dominated possession, swarmed to the ball and generated the most dangerous chance of the early exchanges.

But when Mexico looked like the superior side, the USMNT responded by suddenly slowing the game down and manufacturing its longest possession of the first half. Sebastian Berhalter dropped deep to quarterback the team’s buildup, and players up the pitch freely exchanged possessions to confuse Mexican markers.

Freeman, operating almost as a right winger, threaded a pass to an unmarked Reyna down the channel—on the opposite side flank from where he started the game. The Strasbourg man whipped in a cross, and Hall brilliantly sniffed out the open area to tap-in the USMNT’s opener off a rebound.

After a difficult start, Hall gave the hosts the lead with their first and only shot on target of the first half. Against a team that wasted the few important chances it created, the Stars and Stripes had made the most of theirs.
The opener stunned El Tri, and it was never able to restore its initial superiority. The USMNT, meanwhile, grew into the game and was far and away the better side in the second half.
The USMNT produced a full team effort on Saturday night.  / Taylor Banner/USSF/Getty Images *Ratings provided by FotMob*

GK: Diego Kochen—7.3: A shaky performance from the 20-year-old goalkeeper, who was lucky Santiago Gimenez didn’t pounce on a rebound he left served on a platter. Had some nice passes from deep but also a couple of risky ones. Nice save in the only shot on goal he faced.
RB: Alex Freeman—8.3: Pocketed Orbelín Pineda and was a threat whenever he ventured forward. A clever flick for a charging Reyna started the action of his team’s opener.
CB: Chris Richards—6.8: Dominant in the air and calmly dealt with Mexico’s threat.
CB: Auston Trusty—7.8: Like his partner alongside him, Tursty didn’t put a foot wrong defensively. He was often the first pass out of the back and was effective with his distribution.
LB: Antonee Robinson—7.7: Extremely lucky that a poor clearance didn’t turn into Mexico’s early opener.

RM: Cavan Sullivan—8.3: Came alive in the second half, fearlessly taking on markers and often getting the better of them. His dream night was crowned when he became the youngest goalscorer in USMNT history with a classy finish.
CM: Sebastian Berhalter—7.4: Suffered early, especially out of possession, but the USMNT looked at its best when the midfielder dropped to organize possessions from deep.
